questions.question_html: Let $\hat{a}$ , $\hat{b}$ be unit vectors. If $\vec{c}$ be a vector such that the angle between $\hat{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $\frac{\pi}{12}$ , and $\hat{b}=\vec{c}+2(\vec{c} \times \hat{a})$ , then $|6\vec{c}|^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.explanation_text: $\because \hat{b}=\vec{c}+2(\vec{c} \times \hat{a})$ $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \hat{b} \cdot \vec{c}=|\vec{c}|^{2} \\ \\ & \therefore \hat{b}-\vec{c}=2(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow |\hat{b}|^{2}+|\vec{c}|^{2}-2\hat{b} \cdot \vec{c}=4|\vec{c}|^{2}|\vec{a}|^{2}sin^{2}\frac{\pi}{12} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 1+|\vec{c}|^{2}-2|c|^{2}=4|\vec{c}|^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2\sqrt{2}})^{2} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 1=|\vec{c}|^{2}(3-\sqrt{3}) \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 36|\vec{c}|^{2}=\frac{36}{3-\sqrt{3}}=6(3+\sqrt{3}) \end{aligned}$

$\because \hat{b}=\vec{c}+2(\vec{c} \times \hat{a})$

$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \hat{b} \cdot \vec{c}=|\vec{c}|^{2} \\ \\ & \therefore \hat{b}-\vec{c}=2(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow |\hat{b}|^{2}+|\vec{c}|^{2}-2\hat{b} \cdot \vec{c}=4|\vec{c}|^{2}|\vec{a}|^{2}sin^{2}\frac{\pi}{12} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 1+|\vec{c}|^{2}-2|c|^{2}=4|\vec{c}|^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2\sqrt{2}})^{2} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 1=|\vec{c}|^{2}(3-\sqrt{3}) \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 36|\vec{c}|^{2}=\frac{36}{3-\sqrt{3}}=6(3+\sqrt{3}) \end{aligned}$

questions.question_text: Let $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$ be two unit vectors such that the angle between them is $\frac{\pi}{4}$ . If $\theta$ is the angle between the vectors $(\hat{a}+\hat{b})$ and $(\hat{a}+2\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}))$ , then the value of $164cos^{2}\theta$ is equal to :
questions.question_html: Let $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$ be two unit vectors such that the angle between them is $\frac{\pi}{4}$ . If $\theta$ is the angle between the vectors $(\hat{a}+\hat{b})$ and $(\hat{a}+2\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}))$ , then the value of $164cos^{2}\theta$ is equal to :
questions.explanation_text: $\hat{a}.\hat{b}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $|\hat{a} \times \hat{b}|=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ $\frac{(\hat{a}+\hat{b}).(\hat{a}+2\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}))}{|\hat{a}+\hat{b}||\hat{a}+2\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b})|}=cos\theta$ $\Rightarrow cos\theta=\frac{1+3\hat{a}\hat{b}+2}{|\hat{a}+\hat{b}||\hat{a}+2\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b})|}$ $|\hat{a}+\hat{b}|^{2}=2+\sqrt{2}$ $|\hat{a}+2\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b})|^{2}=1+4+4|\hat{a} \times \hat{b}|^{2}+4\hat{a}\hat{b}$ $=5+4.\frac{1}{2}+\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}}=7+2\sqrt{2}$ So, $cos^{2}\theta=\frac{(3+\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}})^{2}}{(2+\sqrt{2})(7+2\sqrt{2})}=\frac{9\sqrt{2}(5\sqrt{2}+3)}{164}$ $\Rightarrow 164cos^{2}\theta=90+27\sqrt{2}$
questions.explanation_html:
$\hat{a}.\hat{b}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $|\hat{a} \times \hat{b}|=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\frac{(\hat{a}+\hat{b}).(\hat{a}+2\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}))}{|\hat{a}+\hat{b}||\hat{a}+2\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b})|}=cos\theta$

$\Rightarrow cos\theta=\frac{1+3\hat{a}\hat{b}+2}{|\hat{a}+\hat{b}||\hat{a}+2\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b})|}$

$|\hat{a}+\hat{b}|^{2}=2+\sqrt{2}$

$|\hat{a}+2\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b})|^{2}=1+4+4|\hat{a} \times \hat{b}|^{2}+4\hat{a}\hat{b}$

$=5+4.\frac{1}{2}+\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}}=7+2\sqrt{2}$

So, $cos^{2}\theta=\frac{(3+\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}})^{2}}{(2+\sqrt{2})(7+2\sqrt{2})}=\frac{9\sqrt{2}(5\sqrt{2}+3)}{164}$

$\Rightarrow 164cos^{2}\theta=90+27\sqrt{2}$

questions.explanation_text: $\vec{a}=\alpha\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\beta\hat{k}$ , $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=-\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+12\hat{k}$ $|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \alpha & 1 & \beta \\ 3 & -5 & 4 \end{aligned}|=-\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+12\hat{k}$ $4+5\beta=-1 \Rightarrow \beta=-1$ $-5\alpha-3=12 \Rightarrow \alpha=-3$ $\vec{b}-2\vec{a}=3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+4\hat{k}-2(-3\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})$ $\vec{b}-2\vec{a}=9\hat{i}-7\hat{j}+6\hat{k}$ $\vec{b}+\vec{a}=(3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+4\hat{k})+(-3\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})$ $\vec{b}+\vec{a}=-4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ Projection of $\vec{b}-2\vec{a}$ on $\vec{b}+\vec{a}$ is $=\frac{(\vec{b}-2\vec{a}).(\vec{b}+\vec{a})}{|\vec{b}+\vec{a}|}$ $=\frac{28+18}{5}=\frac{46}{5}$
questions.explanation_html:
$\vec{a}=\alpha\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\beta\hat{k}$ , $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$

$\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=-\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+12\hat{k}$

$|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \alpha & 1 & \beta \\ 3 & -5 & 4 \end{aligned}|=-\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+12\hat{k}$

$4+5\beta=-1 \Rightarrow \beta=-1$

$-5\alpha-3=12 \Rightarrow \alpha=-3$

$\vec{b}-2\vec{a}=3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+4\hat{k}-2(-3\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})$

$\vec{b}-2\vec{a}=9\hat{i}-7\hat{j}+6\hat{k}$

$\vec{b}+\vec{a}=(3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+4\hat{k})+(-3\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})$

$\vec{b}+\vec{a}=-4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$

Projection of $\vec{b}-2\vec{a}$ on $\vec{b}+\vec{a}$ is $=\frac{(\vec{b}-2\vec{a}).(\vec{b}+\vec{a})}{|\vec{b}+\vec{a}|}$

$=\frac{28+18}{5}=\frac{46}{5}$

Then

questions.explanation_text: $\because \vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=0$ then $\bar{a}+\vec{c}=-\vec{b}$ then $(\vec{a}+\vec{c}) \times \vec{b}=-\vec{b} \times \bar{b}$ $\therefore \vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{c} \times \vec{b}=\bar{0}\dots(i)$ For $(S1):|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{c} \times \vec{b}|-|\vec{c}|=6(2\sqrt{2}-1)$ $\begin{aligned} & |(\vec{a}+\vec{c}) \times \vec{b}|-|\vec{c}|=6(2\sqrt{2}-1) \\ \\ & |\vec{c}|=6-12\sqrt{2}\text{(not possible)} \end{aligned}$ Hence (S1) is not correct For (S2) : from (i) $\vec{b}+\vec{c}=-\vec{a}$ $\Rightarrow \vec{b} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b}=-\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}$ $\Rightarrow 12+12=-6\sqrt{2} \cdot 2\sqrt{3}cos(\pi-\angleACB)$ $\therefore cos(\angleACB)=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}$ $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \angleACB=cos^{-1}\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} \\ \\ & \therefore S(2)\text{is correct.} \end{aligned}$
questions.explanation_html:
$\because \vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=0$

then $\bar{a}+\vec{c}=-\vec{b}$

then $(\vec{a}+\vec{c}) \times \vec{b}=-\vec{b} \times \bar{b}$

$\therefore \vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{c} \times \vec{b}=\bar{0}\dots(i)$

For $(S1):|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{c} \times \vec{b}|-|\vec{c}|=6(2\sqrt{2}-1)$

$\begin{aligned} & |(\vec{a}+\vec{c}) \times \vec{b}|-|\vec{c}|=6(2\sqrt{2}-1) \\ \\ & |\vec{c}|=6-12\sqrt{2}\text{(not possible)} \end{aligned}$

Hence (S1) is not correct

For (S2) : from (i) $\vec{b}+\vec{c}=-\vec{a}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{b} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b}=-\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}$

$\Rightarrow 12+12=-6\sqrt{2} \cdot 2\sqrt{3}cos(\pi-\angleACB)$

$\therefore cos(\angleACB)=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}$

$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \angleACB=cos^{-1}\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} \\ \\ & \therefore S(2)\text{is correct.} \end{aligned}$

questions.question_text: Let $\vec{a}=\alpha\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=-2\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ , where $\alpha \in R$ . If the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are represented by the vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is $\sqrt{15(\alpha^{2}+4)}$ , then the value of $2|\vec{a}|^{2}+(\vec{a}.\vec{b})|\vec{b}|^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.question_html: Let $\vec{a}=\alpha\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=-2\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ , where $\alpha \in R$ . If the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are represented by the vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is $\sqrt{15(\alpha^{2}+4)}$ , then the value of $2|\vec{a}|^{2}+(\vec{a}.\vec{b})|\vec{b}|^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.explanation_text: $\vec{a}=\alpha\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=-2\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ $\therefore$ $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \alpha & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & \alpha & 1 \end{aligned}|=(2+\alpha)\hat{i}-(\alpha-2)\hat{j}+(\alpha^{2}+4)\hat{k}$ Now $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=\sqrt{15(\alpha^{2}+4)}$ $\Rightarrow (2+\alpha)^{2}+(\alpha-2)^{2}+(\alpha^{2}+4)^{2}=15(\alpha^{2}+4)$ $\Rightarrow \alpha^{4}-5\alpha^{2}-36=0$ $\therefore$ $\alpha= \pm 3$ Now, $2|\vec{a}|^{2}+(\vec{a}-\vec{b})|\vec{b}|^{-2}=2.14-14=14$
questions.explanation_html:
$\vec{a}=\alpha\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=-2\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \alpha & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & \alpha & 1 \end{aligned}|=(2+\alpha)\hat{i}-(\alpha-2)\hat{j}+(\alpha^{2}+4)\hat{k}$

Now $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=\sqrt{15(\alpha^{2}+4)}$

$\Rightarrow (2+\alpha)^{2}+(\alpha-2)^{2}+(\alpha^{2}+4)^{2}=15(\alpha^{2}+4)$

$\Rightarrow \alpha^{4}-5\alpha^{2}-36=0$

$\therefore$ $\alpha= \pm 3$

Now, $2|\vec{a}|^{2}+(\vec{a}-\vec{b})|\vec{b}|^{-2}=2.14-14=14$

questions.explanation_text: $\because$ $\vec{a} \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})=3\vec{b}-\vec{c}=\vec{u}$ $\vec{b} \times (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})=\vec{c}-2\vec{a}=\vec{v}$ $\vec{c} \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{a})=3\vec{b}-2\vec{a}=\vec{w}$ $\therefore$ $\vec{u}+\vec{v}=\vec{w}$ So, vectors $\vec{u}$ , $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{w}$ are coplanar, hence their Scalar triple product will be zero.
questions.explanation_html:
$\because$ $\vec{a} \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})=3\vec{b}-\vec{c}=\vec{u}$

$\vec{b} \times (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})=\vec{c}-2\vec{a}=\vec{v}$

$\vec{c} \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{a})=3\vec{b}-2\vec{a}=\vec{w}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{u}+\vec{v}=\vec{w}$

So, vectors $\vec{u}$ , $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{w}$ are coplanar, hence their Scalar triple product will be zero.

questions.question_text: $\text{Let}\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\text{and}\vec{b}=\alpha\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\text{. If}((\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times \hat{i}) \cdot \hat{k}=\frac{23}{2}\text{, then}|\vec{b} \times 2\hat{j}|$ is equal to :
questions.question_html: $\text{Let}\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\text{and}\vec{b}=\alpha\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\text{. If}((\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times \hat{i}) \cdot \hat{k}=\frac{23}{2}\text{, then}|\vec{b} \times 2\hat{j}|$ is equal to :
questions.explanation_text: Given, $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\alpha\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ Also, $((\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times i).\hat{k}=\frac{23}{2}$ $\Rightarrow ((\vec{a}.\hat{i})\vec{b}-(\vec{b}.\hat{i}).\bar{a}).\hat{k}=\frac{23}{2}$ $\Rightarrow (2.\vec{b}-\alpha.\vec{a}).\hat{k}=\frac{23}{2}$ $\Rightarrow 2.2-5\alpha=\frac{23}{2} \Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{-3}{2}$ Now, $|\vec{b} \times 2j|=|(\alpha\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}+2\hat{k}) \times 2\hat{j}|$ $=|2\alpha\hat{k}+0-4\hat{i}|$ $=\sqrt{4\alpha^{2}+16}$ $=\sqrt{4(\frac{-3}{2})^{2}+16}=5$
questions.explanation_html:
Given, $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\alpha\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$

Also, $((\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times i).\hat{k}=\frac{23}{2}$

$\Rightarrow ((\vec{a}.\hat{i})\vec{b}-(\vec{b}.\hat{i}).\bar{a}).\hat{k}=\frac{23}{2}$

$\Rightarrow (2.\vec{b}-\alpha.\vec{a}).\hat{k}=\frac{23}{2}$

$\Rightarrow 2.2-5\alpha=\frac{23}{2} \Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{-3}{2}$

Now, $|\vec{b} \times 2j|=|(\alpha\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}+2\hat{k}) \times 2\hat{j}|$

$=|2\alpha\hat{k}+0-4\hat{i}|$

$=\sqrt{4\alpha^{2}+16}$

$=\sqrt{4(\frac{-3}{2})^{2}+16}=5$

questions.question_text: Let a vector $\vec{c}$ be coplanar with the vectors $\vec{a}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ . If the vector $\vec{c}$ also satisfies the conditions $\vec{c}.[(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})]=-42$ and $(\vec{c} \times (\vec{a}-\vec{b})).\hat{k}=3$ , then the value of $|\vec{c}|^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.question_html: Let a vector $\vec{c}$ be coplanar with the vectors $\vec{a}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ . If the vector $\vec{c}$ also satisfies the conditions $\vec{c}.[(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})]=-42$ and $(\vec{c} \times (\vec{a}-\vec{b})).\hat{k}=3$ , then the value of $|\vec{c}|^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.explanation_text: Given, $\vec{a}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and let $\vec{c}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$ Now, $\vec{a}+\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}$ and $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \end{aligned}|=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$ $\vec{c}$ is coplanar with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ $\therefore$ $[\vec{c}\vec{a}\vec{b}]=0$ $\Rightarrow |\begin{aligned} x & y & z \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \end{aligned}|=0$ $\Rightarrow x(-2)-y(-1)+z(-3)=0$ $\Rightarrow -2x+y-3z=0$ ..... (1) Now, $(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ $=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 \end{aligned}|$ $=-6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ Given, $\vec{c}.[(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})]=-42$ $\Rightarrow (x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}).(-6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\hat{k})=-42$ $\Rightarrow -6x+3y+5z=-42$ ...... (2) Now, $\vec{a}-\vec{b}=(-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})-(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})$ $=-3\hat{i}+0\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ $\therefore$ $\vec{c} \times (\vec{a}-\vec{b})$ $=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ x & y & z \\ -3 & 0 & 2 \end{aligned}|$ $=2y\hat{i}-\hat{j}(2x+3z)+3y\hat{k}$ Given, $(\vec{c} \times (\vec{a}-\vec{b})).\hat{k}=3$ $\Rightarrow (2y\hat{i}-\hat{j}(2x+3z)+3y\hat{k}).\hat{k}=3$ $\Rightarrow 3y=3$ $\Rightarrow y=1$ Putting value of $y=1$ in equation (1) and (2) we get, $-2x+1-3z=0$ ..... (3) and $-6x+3+5z=-42$ $\Rightarrow -6x+5z=-45$ ..... (4) Solving (3) and (4), we get $x=5$ and $z=-3$ $\therefore$ $\vec{c}=5\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$ $\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|^{2}=5^{2}+1^{2}+(-3)^{2}=35$
questions.explanation_html:
Given,

$\vec{a}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$

$\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$

and let $\vec{c}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$

Now, $\vec{a}+\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}$

and $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \end{aligned}|=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$

$\vec{c}$ is coplanar with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$

$\therefore$ $[\vec{c}\vec{a}\vec{b}]=0$

$\Rightarrow |\begin{aligned} x & y & z \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \end{aligned}|=0$

$\Rightarrow x(-2)-y(-1)+z(-3)=0$

$\Rightarrow -2x+y-3z=0$ ..... (1)

Now, $(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

$=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 \end{aligned}|$

$=-6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$

Given, $\vec{c}.[(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})]=-42$

$\Rightarrow (x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}).(-6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\hat{k})=-42$

$\Rightarrow -6x+3y+5z=-42$ ...... (2)

Now, $\vec{a}-\vec{b}=(-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})-(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})$

$=-3\hat{i}+0\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{c} \times (\vec{a}-\vec{b})$

$=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ x & y & z \\ -3 & 0 & 2 \end{aligned}|$

$=2y\hat{i}-\hat{j}(2x+3z)+3y\hat{k}$

Given,

$(\vec{c} \times (\vec{a}-\vec{b})).\hat{k}=3$

$\Rightarrow (2y\hat{i}-\hat{j}(2x+3z)+3y\hat{k}).\hat{k}=3$

$\Rightarrow 3y=3$

$\Rightarrow y=1$

Putting value of $y=1$ in equation (1) and (2) we get,

$-2x+1-3z=0$ ..... (3)

and $-6x+3+5z=-42$

$\Rightarrow -6x+5z=-45$ ..... (4)

Solving (3) and (4), we get

$x=5$ and $z=-3$

$\therefore$ $\vec{c}=5\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$

$\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|^{2}=5^{2}+1^{2}+(-3)^{2}=35$

(ii) and $a_{1}-2a_{3}=13$ ..... (iii) From eq. (i) and (iii) : $a_{1}=3$ and $a_{3}=-5$ $\therefore$ $\vec{a}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$ $\therefore$ projection of $\vec{a}$ on $2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}=\frac{6+4-5}{3}=\frac{5}{3}$
questions.explanation_html:
Let $\vec{a}=a_{1}\hat{i}+a_{2}\hat{j}+a_{3}\hat{k}$

and $\vec{a}.(3\hat{i}-\frac{1}{2}\hat{j}+2\hat{k})=0 \Rightarrow 3a_{1}+\frac{a_{2}}{2}+2a_{3}=0$ ..... (i)

and $\vec{a} \times (2\hat{i}+\hat{k})=2\hat{i}-13\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$

$\Rightarrow a_{2}\hat{i}+(2a_{3}-a_{1})\hat{j}-2a_{2}\hat{k}=2\hat{i}-13\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$

and $a_{1}-2a_{3}=13$ ..... (iii)

From eq. (i) and (iii) : $a_{1}=3$ and $a_{3}=-5$

$\therefore$ $\vec{a}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$

$\therefore$ projection of $\vec{a}$ on $2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}=\frac{6+4-5}{3}=\frac{5}{3}$

questions.question_text: Let $\vec{a}=a_{1}\hat{i}+a_{2}\hat{j}+a_{3}\hat{k}$ $a_{i}>0$ , $i=1,2,3$ be a vector which makes equal angles with the coordinate axes OX, OY and OZ. questions.explanation_html:
$cos^{2}\alpha+cos^{2}\beta+cos^{2}\gamma=1 \Rightarrow cos^{2}\alpha=\frac{1}{3} \Rightarrow cos\alpha=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$\vec{a}=\frac{\lambda}{3}(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}),\lambda>0$

$\frac{\lambda}{\sqrt{3}}\frac{(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}).(3\hat{i}+4\hat{j})}{\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}}=7$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\lambda}{\sqrt{3}}(3+4)=7 \times 5$

$\therefore$ $\lambda=5\sqrt{3}$

$\vec{a}=5(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})$

Let $\vec{b}=p\hat{i}+q\hat{j}+r\hat{k}$

$\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ and $[\vec{a}\vec{b}\hat{i}]=0$

$\Rightarrow p+q+r=0$ ..... (i)

& $|\begin{aligned} p & q & r \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \end{aligned}|=0 \Rightarrow \begin{aligned} q=r \\ p=-2r \end{aligned}$

$\vec{b}=-2r\hat{i}+r\hat{j}+r\hat{k}$

$\vec{b}=r(-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})$

Now $|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|$

$5\sqrt{3}=|r|\sqrt{b} \Rightarrow |r|=\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ Projection of $\vec{b}$ on $3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}=|\frac{\vec{b}.(3\hat{i}+4\hat{j})}{\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}}|$

$=|r|\frac{(-6+4)}{5}=|\frac{-2r}{5}|$

Projection $=\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}$

$\therefore$ B is correct.

questions.question_text: Let $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}$ , $\lambda$ $\in$ R. If $\vec{a}$ is a vector such that $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=13\hat{i}-\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ and $\vec{a}.\vec{b}+21=0$ , then $(\vec{b}-\vec{a}).(\hat{k}-\hat{j})+(\vec{b}+\vec{a}).(\hat{i}-\hat{k})$ is equal to _____________.
questions.question_html: Let $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}$ , $\lambda$ $\in$ R. If $\vec{a}$ is a vector such that $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=13\hat{i}-\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ and $\vec{a}.\vec{b}+21=0$ , then $(\vec{b}-\vec{a}).(\hat{k}-\hat{j})+(\vec{b}+\vec{a}).(\hat{i}-\hat{k})$ is equal to _____________.
questions.explanation_text: Let $\vec{a}=x\hat{i}=y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$ So, $|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ x & y & z \\ 1 & 1 & \lambda \end{aligned}|=\hat{i}(\lambda y-z)+\hat{j}(z-\lambda x)+\hat{k}(x-y)$ $\Rightarrow \lambda y-z=13,z-\lambda x=-1,x-y=-4$ and $x+y+\lambda z=-21$ $\Rightarrow$ Clearly, $\lambda=3$ , $x=-2$ , $y=2$ and $z=-7$ So, $\vec{b}-\vec{a}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+10\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}+\vec{a}=-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ $\Rightarrow (\vec{b}-\vec{a}).(\hat{k}-\hat{j})+(\vec{b}+\vec{a}).(\hat{i}-\hat{k})=11+3=14$
questions.explanation_html:
Let $\vec{a}=x\hat{i}=y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$

So, $|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ x & y & z \\ 1 & 1 & \lambda \end{aligned}|=\hat{i}(\lambda y-z)+\hat{j}(z-\lambda x)+\hat{k}(x-y)$

$\Rightarrow \lambda y-z=13,z-\lambda x=-1,x-y=-4$

and $x+y+\lambda z=-21$

$\Rightarrow$ Clearly, $\lambda=3$ , $x=-2$ , $y=2$ and $z=-7$

So, $\vec{b}-\vec{a}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+10\hat{k}$

and $\vec{b}+\vec{a}=-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$

$\Rightarrow (\vec{b}-\vec{a}).(\hat{k}-\hat{j})+(\vec{b}+\vec{a}).(\hat{i}-\hat{k})=11+3=14$

questions.question_text: Let $\vec{a},\vec{b},\vec{c}$ be three coplanar concurrent vectors such that angles between any two of them is same. If the product of their magnitudes is 14 and $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})+(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \cdot (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})+(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \cdot (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})=168$ , then $|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|+|\vec{c}|$ is equal to :
questions.question_html: Let $\vec{a},\vec{b},\vec{c}$ be three coplanar concurrent vectors such that angles between any two of them is same. If the product of their magnitudes is 14 and $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})+(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \cdot (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})+(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \cdot (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})=168$ , then $|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|+|\vec{c}|$ is equal to :
questions.explanation_text: $|\vec{a}||\vec{b}||\vec{c}|=14$ $\begin{aligned} & \vec{a} \wedge \vec{b}=\vec{b} \wedge \vec{c}=\vec{c} \wedge \vec{a}=\theta=\frac{2\pi}{3} \\ \\ & \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=-\frac{1}{2}|\vec{a}||\vec{b}| \\ \\ & \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}=-\frac{1}{2}|\vec{b}||\vec{c}| \\ \\ & \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}=-\frac{1}{2}|\vec{c}||\vec{a}| \end{aligned}$ Now, $\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} & (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})+(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \cdot (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})+(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \cdot (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \\ \\ & =168...(i) \\ \\ & (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})=(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})-(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c})|\vec{b}|^{2} \\ \\ & =\frac{1}{4}|\vec{b}|^{2}|\vec{a}||\vec{c}|+\frac{1}{2}|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|^{2}|\vec{c}| \\ \\ & =\frac{3}{4}|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|^{2}|\vec{c}|...(ii) \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$ Similarly $(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \cdot (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})=\frac{3}{4}|\vec{a}||\vec{b}||\vec{c}|^{2}...(iii)$ $(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \cdot (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})=\frac{3}{4}|\vec{a}|^{2}|\vec{b}||\vec{c}|...(iv)$ Substitute (ii), (iii), (iv) in (i) $\frac{3}{4}|\vec{a}||\vec{b}||\vec{c}|[|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|+|\vec{c}|]=168$ $\frac{3}{4} \times 14[|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|+|\vec{c}|]=168$ $|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|+|\vec{c}|=16$
questions.explanation_html:
$|\vec{a}||\vec{b}||\vec{c}|=14$

$\begin{aligned} & \vec{a} \wedge \vec{b}=\vec{b} \wedge \vec{c}=\vec{c} \wedge \vec{a}=\theta=\frac{2\pi}{3} \\ \\ & \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=-\frac{1}{2}|\vec{a}||\vec{b}| \\ \\ & \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}=-\frac{1}{2}|\vec{b}||\vec{c}| \\ \\ & \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}=-\frac{1}{2}|\vec{c}||\vec{a}| \end{aligned}$

Now,

$\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} & (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})+(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \cdot (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})+(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \cdot (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \\ \\ & =168...(i) \\ \\ & (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})=(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})-(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c})|\vec{b}|^{2} \\ \\ & =\frac{1}{4}|\vec{b}|^{2}|\vec{a}||\vec{c}|+\frac{1}{2}|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|^{2}|\vec{c}| \\ \\ & =\frac{3}{4}|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|^{2}|\vec{c}|...(ii) \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$

Similarly $(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \cdot (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})=\frac{3}{4}|\vec{a}||\vec{b}||\vec{c}|^{2}...(iii)$

$(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \cdot (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})=\frac{3}{4}|\vec{a}|^{2}|\vec{b}||\vec{c}|...(iv)$

Substitute (ii), (iii), (iv) in (i)

$\frac{3}{4}|\vec{a}||\vec{b}||\vec{c}|[|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|+|\vec{c}|]=168$

$\frac{3}{4} \times 14[|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|+|\vec{c}|]=168$

$|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|+|\vec{c}|=16$

questions.explanation_text: Given : $\vec{a}=(\alpha,1,-1)$ and $\vec{b}=(2,1,-\alpha)$ $\vec{c}=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \alpha & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & -\alpha \end{aligned}|$ $=(-\alpha+1)\hat{i}+(\alpha^{2}-2)\hat{j}+(\alpha-2)\hat{k}$ Projection of $\vec{c}$ on $\vec{d}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$ $=|\vec{c}.\frac{\vec{d}}{|d|}|=30$ {Given} $\Rightarrow =|\frac{\alpha-1-4+2\alpha^{2}-2\alpha+4}{\sqrt{1+4+4}}|=30$ On solving $\alpha=\frac{-13}{2}$ (Rejected as $\alpha>0$ ) and $\alpha=7$

Given : $\vec{a}=(\alpha,1,-1)$ and $\vec{b}=(2,1,-\alpha)$

$\vec{c}=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \alpha & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & -\alpha \end{aligned}|$

$=(-\alpha+1)\hat{i}+(\alpha^{2}-2)\hat{j}+(\alpha-2)\hat{k}$

Projection of $\vec{c}$ on $\vec{d}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$

$=|\vec{c}.\frac{\vec{d}}{|d|}|=30$ {Given}

$\Rightarrow =|\frac{\alpha-1-4+2\alpha^{2}-2\alpha+4}{\sqrt{1+4+4}}|=30$

On solving $\alpha=\frac{-13}{2}$ (Rejected as $\alpha>0$ )

and $\alpha=7$

(i) and $|\vec{a}.\vec{b}|=|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$ $|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|cos\theta=|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|sin\theta$ $\Rightarrow tan\theta=1$ $\therefore$ $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ By (i) $|\vec{b}|=8$ Now $\vec{c}=2\sqrt{2}(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})-2\vec{b}$ $\Rightarrow \vec{c}.\vec{b}=-2|\vec{b}|^{2}=-128$ ...... $\because$ $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ be the vectors along the diagonals of a parallelogram having area 2 $\sqrt{2}$ .

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=2\sqrt{2}$

$|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|sin\theta=4\sqrt{2}$

$\Rightarrow |\vec{b}|sin\theta=4\sqrt{2}$ ..... (i)

and $|\vec{a}.\vec{b}|=|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$

$|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|cos\theta=|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|sin\theta$

From (ii) and (iii)

$\Rightarrow cos\alpha=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question_text: Let $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$ be two unit vectors such that $|(\hat{a}+\hat{b})+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b})|=2$ . If $\theta$ $\in$ (0, $\pi$ ) is the angle between $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$ , then among the statements : (S1) : $2|\hat{a} \times \hat{b}|=|\hat{a}-\hat{b}|$ (S2) : The projection of $\hat{a}$ on ( $\hat{a}$ + $\hat{b}$ ) is $\frac{1}{2}$
questions.question_html:
Let $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$ be two unit vectors such that $|(\hat{a}+\hat{b})+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b})|=2$ . If $\theta$ $\in$ (0, $\pi$ ) is the angle between $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$ , then among the statements :

(S1) : $2|\hat{a} \times \hat{b}|=|\hat{a}-\hat{b}|$

(S2) : The projection of $\hat{a}$ on ( $\hat{a}$ + $\hat{b}$ ) is $\frac{1}{2}$

options.label: A
options.html: Only (S1) is true.

options.label: B
options.html: Only (S2) is true.

options.label: C
options.html: Both (S1) and (S2) are true.

options.label: D
options.html: Both (S1) and (S2) are false.

questions.explanation_text: $|\hat{a}+\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b})|=2,\theta \in (0,\pi)$ $\Rightarrow |\hat{a}+\hat{b}+2(\hat{a} \times \hat{b})|^{2}=4$ $\Rightarrow |\hat{a}|^{2}+|\hat{b}|^{2}+4|\hat{a} \times \hat{b}|^{2}+2\hat{a}.\hat{b}=4$ $\therefore$ $cos\theta=cos2\theta$ $\therefore$ $\theta=\frac{2\pi}{3}$ where $\theta$ is angle between $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$ . $\therefore$ $2|\hat{a} \times \hat{b}|=\sqrt{3}=|\hat{a}-\hat{b}|$ (S1) is correct. And projection of $\hat{a}$ on $(\hat{a}+\hat{b})=|\frac{\hat{a}.(\hat{a}+\hat{b})}{|\hat{a}+\hat{b}|}|=\frac{1}{2}$ (S2) is correct.

questions.question_text: Let $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ , $\vec{c}$ be three non-coplanar vectors such that $\vec{a}$ $\times$ $\vec{b}$ = 4 $\vec{c}$ , $\vec{b}$ $\times$ $\vec{c}$ = 9 $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ $\times$ $\vec{a}$ = $\alpha$ $\vec{b}$ , $\alpha$ > 0. If $|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|+|\vec{c}|=\frac{1}{36}$ , then $\alpha$ is equal to __________.
questions.question_html: Let $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ , $\vec{c}$ be three non-coplanar vectors such that $\vec{a}$ $\times$ $\vec{b}$ = 4 $\vec{c}$ , $\vec{b}$ $\times$ $\vec{c}$ = 9 $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ $\times$ $\vec{a}$ = $\alpha$ $\vec{b}$ , $\alpha$ > 0. If $|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|+|\vec{c}|=\frac{1}{36}$ , then $\alpha$ is equal to __________.
questions.explanation_text: Given, $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=4.\vec{c}$ ..... (i) $\vec{b} \times \vec{c}=9.\vec{a}$ ..... (ii) $\vec{c} \times \vec{a}=\alpha.\vec{b}$ .... (iii) Taking dot products with $\vec{c},\vec{a},\vec{b}$ we get $\vec{a}.\vec{b}=\vec{b}.\vec{c}=\vec{c}.\vec{a}=0$ Hence, (i) $\Rightarrow |\vec{a}|.|\vec{b}|=4.|\vec{c}|$ ..... (iv) (ii) $\Rightarrow |\vec{b}|.|\vec{c}|=9.|\vec{a}|$ ..... (v) (iii) $\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|.|\vec{a}|=\alpha.|\vec{b}|$ .... (vi) Multiplying (iv), (v) and (vi) $\Rightarrow |\vec{a}|.|\vec{b}|.|\vec{c}|=36\alpha$ ..... (vii) Dividing (vii) by (iv) $\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|^{2}=9\alpha \Rightarrow |\vec{c}|=3\sqrt{\alpha}$ ..... (viii) Dividing (vii) by (v) $\Rightarrow |\vec{a}|^{2}=4\alpha \Rightarrow |\vec{a}|=2\sqrt{\alpha}$ Dividing (viii) by (vi) $\Rightarrow |\vec{b}|^{2}=36 \Rightarrow |\vec{b}|=6$ Now, as given, $3\sqrt{\alpha}+2\sqrt{\alpha}+6=\frac{1}{36} \Rightarrow \sqrt{\alpha}=\frac{-43}{36}$
questions.explanation_html:
Given,

$\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=4.\vec{c}$ ..... (i)

$\vec{b} \times \vec{c}=9.\vec{a}$ ..... (ii)

$\vec{c} \times \vec{a}=\alpha.\vec{b}$ .... (iii)

Taking dot products with $\vec{c},\vec{a},\vec{b}$ we get

$\vec{a}.\vec{b}=\vec{b}.\vec{c}=\vec{c}.\vec{a}=0$

Hence,

(i) $\Rightarrow |\vec{a}|.|\vec{b}|=4.|\vec{c}|$ ..... (iv)

(ii) $\Rightarrow |\vec{b}|.|\vec{c}|=9.|\vec{a}|$ ..... (v)

(iii) $\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|.|\vec{a}|=\alpha.|\vec{b}|$ .... (vi)

Multiplying (iv), (v) and (vi)

$\Rightarrow |\vec{a}|.|\vec{b}|.|\vec{c}|=36\alpha$ ..... (vii)

Dividing (vii) by (iv) $\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|^{2}=9\alpha \Rightarrow |\vec{c}|=3\sqrt{\alpha}$ ..... (viii)

Dividing (vii) by (v) $\Rightarrow |\vec{a}|^{2}=4\alpha \Rightarrow |\vec{a}|=2\sqrt{\alpha}$

Dividing (viii) by (vi) $\Rightarrow |\vec{b}|^{2}=36 \Rightarrow |\vec{b}|=6$

Now, as given, $3\sqrt{\alpha}+2\sqrt{\alpha}+6=\frac{1}{36} \Rightarrow \sqrt{\alpha}=\frac{-43}{36}$

questions.explanation_text: $|(\vec{a}-\vec{b}) \times (\vec{a}+\vec{b})|^{2}+4(\vec{a}.\vec{b})^{2}$ $\Rightarrow |\vec{a} \times \vec{a}+\vec{a} \times \vec{b}-\vec{b} \times \vec{a}-\vec{b} \times \vec{b}|^{2}+4(\vec{a}.\vec{b})^{2}$ $\Rightarrow |2(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})|^{2}+4(\vec{a}.\vec{b})^{2}$ $\Rightarrow 4(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})^{2}+(\vec{a}.\vec{b})^{2}$ $\Rightarrow 4|\vec{a}|^{2}|\vec{b}|^{2}=4.16.9=576$

questions.question_html: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ . If $\vec{c}$ is a vector such that $\vec{a} \times \vec{c}=\vec{b}$ and $\vec{a}.\vec{c}=3$ , then $\vec{a}.(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$ is equal to :
questions.explanation_text: $|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{3}$ ; $\vec{a}.\vec{c}=3$ ; $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ , $\vec{a} \times \vec{c}=\vec{b}$ Cross with $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{a} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{c})=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$ $\Rightarrow (\vec{a}.\vec{c})\vec{a}-a^{2}\vec{c}=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$ $\Rightarrow 3\vec{a}-3\vec{c}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ $\Rightarrow 3\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+3\hat{k}-3\vec{c}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ $\Rightarrow \vec{c}=\frac{5\hat{i}}{3}+\frac{2\hat{j}}{3}+\frac{2\hat{k}}{3}$ $\therefore$ $\vec{a}.(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})=(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}).\vec{c}=\frac{-10}{3}+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{3}=-2$
questions.explanation_html:
$|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{3}$ ; $\vec{a}.\vec{c}=3$ ; $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ , $\vec{a} \times \vec{c}=\vec{b}$

Cross with $\vec{a}$ ,

$\vec{a} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{c})=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$

$\Rightarrow (\vec{a}.\vec{c})\vec{a}-a^{2}\vec{c}=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$

$\Rightarrow 3\vec{a}-3\vec{c}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$

$\Rightarrow 3\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+3\hat{k}-3\vec{c}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{c}=\frac{5\hat{i}}{3}+\frac{2\hat{j}}{3}+\frac{2\hat{k}}{3}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{a}.(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})=(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}).\vec{c}=\frac{-10}{3}+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{3}=-2$

questions.question_text: Let $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ . Let a vector $\vec{v}$ be in the plane containing $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ . If $\vec{v}$ is perpendicular to the vector $3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and its projection on $\vec{a}$ is 19 units, then $|2\vec{v}|^{2}$ is equal to _____________.
questions.question_html: Let $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ . Let a vector $\vec{v}$ be in the plane containing $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ . If $\vec{v}$ is perpendicular to the vector $3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and its projection on $\vec{a}$ is 19 units, then $|2\vec{v}|^{2}$ is equal to _____________.
questions.explanation_text: $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ $\vec{c}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ $\vec{v}=x\vec{a}+y\vec{b}$ $\vec{v}(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})=0$ $\vec{v}.\hat{a}=19$ $\vec{v}=\lambda\vec{c} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ $\vec{v}=\lambda[(\vec{c}.\vec{b})\vec{a}-(\vec{c}.\vec{a})\vec{b}]$ $=\lambda[(3+4+1)(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})-(\frac{6-2-2}{2})(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ $=\lambda[16\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+16\hat{k}-2\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+2\hat{k}]$ $\vec{v}=\lambda[14\hat{i}-12\hat{j}+18\hat{k}]$ $\lambda[14\hat{i}-12\hat{j}+18\hat{k}].\frac{(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})}{\sqrt{4+1+4}}=19$ $\lambda\frac{[28+12+36]}{3}=19$ $\lambda(\frac{76}{3})=19$ $4\lambda=3 \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{3}{4}$ $|2v^{2}|=|2 \times \frac{3}{4}(14\hat{i}-12\hat{j}+18\hat{k})|^{2}$ $\frac{9}{4} \times 4(7\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+9\hat{k})^{2}$ $=9(49+36+81)$ $=9(166)$ $=1494$
questions.explanation_html:
$\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$

$\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$

$\vec{c}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$

$\vec{v}=x\vec{a}+y\vec{b}$

$\vec{v}(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})=0$

$\vec{v}.\hat{a}=19$

$\vec{v}=\lambda\vec{c} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

$\vec{v}=\lambda[(\vec{c}.\vec{b})\vec{a}-(\vec{c}.\vec{a})\vec{b}]$

$=\lambda[(3+4+1)(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})-(\frac{6-2-2}{2})(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})$

$=\lambda[16\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+16\hat{k}-2\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+2\hat{k}]$

$\vec{v}=\lambda[14\hat{i}-12\hat{j}+18\hat{k}]$

$\lambda[14\hat{i}-12\hat{j}+18\hat{k}].\frac{(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})}{\sqrt{4+1+4}}=19$

$\lambda\frac{[28+12+36]}{3}=19$

$\lambda(\frac{76}{3})=19$

$4\lambda=3 \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{3}{4}$

$|2v^{2}|=|2 \times \frac{3}{4}(14\hat{i}-12\hat{j}+18\hat{k})|^{2}$

$\frac{9}{4} \times 4(7\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+9\hat{k})^{2}$

$=9(49+36+81)$

$=9(166)$

$=1494$

questions.question_html: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k},\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}=\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ be three vectors such that $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\vec{c}$ and $\vec{a}.\vec{b}=1$ . If the length of projection vector of the vector $\vec{b}$ on the vector $\vec{a} \times \vec{c}$ is l, then the value of 3l2 is equal to _____________.
questions.explanation_text: $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\vec{c}$ Take Dot with $\vec{c}$ $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}).\vec{c}=|\vec{c}|^{2}=2$ Projection of $\vec{b}$ or $\vec{a} \times \vec{c}=l$ $\frac{|\vec{b}.(\vec{a} \times \vec{c})|}{|\vec{a} \times \vec{c}|}=l$ $\therefore$ $l=\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \Rightarrow l^{2}=\frac{4}{6}$ $3l^{2}=2$
questions.explanation_html:
$\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\vec{c}$

Take Dot with $\vec{c}$

$(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}).\vec{c}=|\vec{c}|^{2}=2$

Projection of $\vec{b}$ or $\vec{a} \times \vec{c}=l$

$\frac{|\vec{b}.(\vec{a} \times \vec{c})|}{|\vec{a} \times \vec{c}|}=l$

$\therefore$ $l=\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \Rightarrow l^{2}=\frac{4}{6}$

$3l^{2}=2$

If $\vec{c}.(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k})$ = 8 then the value of $\vec{c}$ . $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ is equal to __________.
questions.question_html:
Let $\vec{c}$ be a vector perpendicular to the vectors, $\vec{a}$ = $\hat{i}$ + $\hat{j}$ $-$ $\hat{k}$ and
$\vec{b}$ = $\hat{i}$ + 2 $\hat{j}$ + $\hat{k}$ . If $\vec{c}.(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k})$ = 8 then the value of
$\vec{c}$ . $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ is equal to __________.
questions.explanation_text: $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \end{aligned}|=(3,-2,1)$ $\vec{c}\perp\vec{a},\vec{c}\perp\vec{b} \Rightarrow C||\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$ $\vec{c}=\lambda(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ $\Rightarrow \vec{c}=\lambda(3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ Given, $\vec{c}.(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k})=8$ $\Rightarrow 3\lambda-2\lambda+3\lambda=8$ $\Rightarrow 4\lambda=8 \Rightarrow \lambda=2$ $\therefore$ $\vec{c}=6\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ $\vec{c}.(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})=[\vec{c}\vec{a}\vec{b}]=|\begin{aligned} 6 & -4 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \end{aligned}|$ $\Rightarrow$ 18 + 8 + 2 = 28
questions.explanation_html:
$\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \end{aligned}|=(3,-2,1)$

$\vec{c}\perp\vec{a},\vec{c}\perp\vec{b} \Rightarrow C||\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$

$\vec{c}=\lambda(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

$\Rightarrow \vec{c}=\lambda(3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})$

Given, $\vec{c}.(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k})=8$

$\Rightarrow 3\lambda-2\lambda+3\lambda=8$

$\Rightarrow 4\lambda=8 \Rightarrow \lambda=2$

$\therefore$ $\vec{c}=6\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$

$\vec{c}.(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})=[\vec{c}\vec{a}\vec{b}]=|\begin{aligned} 6 & -4 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \end{aligned}|$

$\Rightarrow$ 18 + 8 + 2 = 28

questions.explanation_text: Suppose $\vec{r}=x\vec{a}+y\vec{b}+2\vec{c}$ and $|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=|\vec{c}|=k$ $\vec{a} \times {(\vec{r}-\vec{b}) \times \vec{a}}+\vec{b} \times {(\vec{r}-\vec{c}) \times \vec{b}}+\vec{c} \times {(\vec{r}-\vec{a}) \times \vec{c}}=\vec{0}$ $\Rightarrow k^{2}(\vec{r}-\vec{b})-k^{2}x\vec{a}+k^{2}(\vec{r}-\vec{c})-k^{2}y\vec{b}+k^{2}(\vec{r}-\vec{a})-k^{2}z\vec{c}=\vec{0}$ $\Rightarrow 3\vec{r}-(\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c})-\vec{r}=\vec{0}$ $\Rightarrow \vec{r}=\frac{\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}}{2}$

Suppose $\vec{r}=x\vec{a}+y\vec{b}+2\vec{c}$

$\Rightarrow k^{2}(\vec{r}-\vec{b})-k^{2}x\vec{a}+k^{2}(\vec{r}-\vec{c})-k^{2}y\vec{b}+k^{2}(\vec{r}-\vec{a})-k^{2}z\vec{c}=\vec{0}$

questions.question_text: Let $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ be three vectors such that $\vec{a}$ = $\vec{b}$ $\times$ ( $\vec{b}$ $\times$ $\vec{c}$ ). If magnitudes of the vectors $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ are $\sqrt{2}$ , 1 and 2 respectively and the angle between $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $\theta(0<\theta<\frac{\pi}{2})$ , then the value of 1 + tan $\theta$ is equal to :
questions.question_html: Let $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ be three vectors such that $\vec{a}$ = $\vec{b}$ $\times$ ( $\vec{b}$ $\times$ $\vec{c}$ ). If magnitudes of the vectors $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ are $\sqrt{2}$ , 1 and 2 respectively and the angle between $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $\theta(0<\theta<\frac{\pi}{2})$ , then the value of 1 + tan $\theta$ is equal to :
questions.explanation_text: $\vec{a}=(\vec{b}.\vec{c})\vec{b}-(\vec{b}.\vec{b})\vec{c}$ $=1.2cos\theta\vec{b}-\vec{c}$ $\Rightarrow \vec{a}=2cos\theta\vec{b}-\vec{c}$ $|\vec{a}|^{2}=(2cos\theta)^{2}+2^{2}-2.2cos\theta\vec{b}.\vec{c}$ $\Rightarrow 2=4cos^{2}\theta+4-4cos\theta.2cos\theta$ $\Rightarrow -2=-4cos^{2}\theta$ $\Rightarrow cos^{2}\theta=\frac{1}{2}$ $\Rightarrow sec^{2}\theta=2$ $\Rightarrow tan^{2}\theta=1$ $\Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ $\therefore$ $1+tan\theta=2$
questions.explanation_html:
$\vec{a}=(\vec{b}.\vec{c})\vec{b}-(\vec{b}.\vec{b})\vec{c}$

$=1.2cos\theta\vec{b}-\vec{c}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{a}=2cos\theta\vec{b}-\vec{c}$

$|\vec{a}|^{2}=(2cos\theta)^{2}+2^{2}-2.2cos\theta\vec{b}.\vec{c}$

$\Rightarrow 2=4cos^{2}\theta+4-4cos\theta.2cos\theta$

$\Rightarrow -2=-4cos^{2}\theta$

$\Rightarrow cos^{2}\theta=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow sec^{2}\theta=2$

$\Rightarrow tan^{2}\theta=1$

questions.question_text: Let the vectors $(2+a+b)\hat{i}+(a+2b+c)\hat{j}-(b+c)\hat{k},(1+b)\hat{i}+2b\hat{j}-b\hat{k}$ and $(2+b)\hat{i}+2b\hat{j}+(1-b)\hat{k}$ , $a,b,c, \in R$ be co-planar. Then which of the following is true?
questions.question_html:
Let the vectors

$(2+a+b)\hat{i}+(a+2b+c)\hat{j}-(b+c)\hat{k},(1+b)\hat{i}+2b\hat{j}-b\hat{k}$ and $(2+b)\hat{i}+2b\hat{j}+(1-b)\hat{k}$ , $a,b,c, \in R$

be co-planar. Then which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.html: 2b = a + c

options.label: B
options.html: 3c = a + b

options.label: D
options.html: 2a = b + c

questions.explanation_text: If the vectors are co-planar, $|\begin{aligned} a+b+2 & a+2b+c & -b-c \\ b+1 & 2b & -b \\ b+2 & 2b & 1-b \end{aligned}|=0$ Now, $R_{3} \rightarrow R_{3}-R_{2},R_{1} \rightarrow R_{1}-R_{2}$ So, $|\begin{aligned} a+1 & a+c & -c \\ b+1 & 2b & -b \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{aligned}|=0$ $=(a+1)2b-(a+c)(2b+1)-c(-2b)$ $=2ab+2b-2ab-a-2bc-c+2bc$ $=2b-a-c=0$
questions.explanation_html:
If the vectors are co-planar,

$|\begin{aligned} a+b+2 & a+2b+c & -b-c \\ b+1 & 2b & -b \\ b+2 & 2b & 1-b \end{aligned}|=0$

Now, $R_{3} \rightarrow R_{3}-R_{2},R_{1} \rightarrow R_{1}-R_{2}$

So, $|\begin{aligned} a+1 & a+c & -c \\ b+1 & 2b & -b \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{aligned}|=0$

$=(a+1)2b-(a+c)(2b+1)-c(-2b)$

$=2ab+2b-2ab-a-2bc-c+2bc$

$=2b-a-c=0$

If $\vec{c}$ is a vector such that $\vec{a}.\vec{c}=|\vec{c}|,|\vec{c}-\vec{a}|=2\sqrt{2}$ and the angle between $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ and $\vec{c}$ is $\frac{\pi}{6}$ , then the value of $|(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times \vec{c}|$ is :

$|\vec{a}|=3=a;\vec{a}.\vec{c}=c$

Now, $|\vec{c}-\vec{a}|=2\sqrt{2}$

$=3/2$

questions.question_text: Let O be the origin. Let $\vec{OP}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\vec{OQ}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3x\hat{k}$ , x, y $\in$ R, x > 0, be such that $|\vec{PQ}|=\sqrt{20}$ and the vector $\vec{OP}$ is perpendicular $\vec{OQ}$ . If $\vec{OR}$ = $3\hat{i}+z\hat{j}-7\hat{k}$ , z $\in$ R, is coplanar with $\vec{OP}$ and $\vec{OQ}$ , then the value of x 2 + y 2 + z 2 is equal to :
questions.question_html: Let O be the origin. Let $\vec{OP}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\vec{OQ}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3x\hat{k}$ , x, y $\in$ R, x > 0, be such that $|\vec{PQ}|=\sqrt{20}$ and the vector $\vec{OP}$ is perpendicular $\vec{OQ}$ . If $\vec{OR}$ = $3\hat{i}+z\hat{j}-7\hat{k}$ , z $\in$ R, is coplanar with $\vec{OP}$ and $\vec{OQ}$ , then the value of x2 + y2 + z2 is equal to :
questions.explanation_text: $\vec{OP}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ $\vec{OP}\perp\vec{OQ}$ $\vec{OQ}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3x\hat{k}$ $\vec{PQ}=(-1-x)\hat{i}+(2-y)\hat{j}+(3x+1)\hat{k}$ $|\vec{PQ}|=\sqrt{(-1-x)^{2}+(2-y)^{2}+(3x+1)^{2}}$ $\sqrt{20}=\sqrt{(-1-x)^{2}+(2-y)^{2}+(3x+1)^{2}}$ 20 = 1 + x 2 + 2x + 4 + y 2 $-$ 4y + 9x 2 + 1 + 6x 20 = 10x 2 + y 2 + 8x + 6 $-$ 4y 20 = 10x 2 + 4x 2 + 8x + 6 $-$ 8x 14 = 14x 2 $\Rightarrow$ x 2 = 1 Also, $\vec{OP}.\vec{OQ}=0$ $-x+2y-3x=0$ $4x=2y$ y = 2x $\therefore$ y 2 = 4x 2 $\Rightarrow$ y 2 = 4 x = 1 as x > 0 and y = 2 $\therefore$ $|\begin{aligned} x & y & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 3x \\ 3 & z & -7 \end{aligned}|=0$ $\Rightarrow$ $|\begin{aligned} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & z & -7 \end{aligned}|$ = 0 $\Rightarrow$ 1( $-$ 14 $-$ 3z) $-$ 2(7 $-$ 9) $-$ 1( $-$ z $-$ 6) = 0 $\Rightarrow$ $-$ 14 $-$ 3z + 4 + z + 6 = 0 $\Rightarrow$ 2z = $-$ 4 $\Rightarrow$ z = $-$ 2 $\therefore$ x 2 + y 2 + z 2 = 9
questions.explanation_html:
$\vec{OP}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}-\hat{k}$

$\vec{OP}\perp\vec{OQ}$

$\vec{OQ}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3x\hat{k}$

$\vec{PQ}=(-1-x)\hat{i}+(2-y)\hat{j}+(3x+1)\hat{k}$

$|\vec{PQ}|=\sqrt{(-1-x)^{2}+(2-y)^{2}+(3x+1)^{2}}$

$\sqrt{20}=\sqrt{(-1-x)^{2}+(2-y)^{2}+(3x+1)^{2}}$

20 = 1 + x2 + 2x + 4 + y2 $-$ 4y + 9x2 + 1 + 6x

20 = 10x2 + y2 + 8x + 6 $-$ 4y

20 = 10x2 + 4x2 + 8x + 6 $-$ 8x

14 = 14x2 $\Rightarrow$ x2 = 1

Also, $\vec{OP}.\vec{OQ}=0$

$-x+2y-3x=0$

$4x=2y$

y = 2x

$\therefore$ y2 = 4x2 $\Rightarrow$ y2 = 4

x = 1 as x > 0 and y = 2

$\therefore$ $|\begin{aligned} x & y & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 3x \\ 3 & z & -7 \end{aligned}|=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $|\begin{aligned} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & z & -7 \end{aligned}|$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 1( $-$ 14 $-$ 3z) $-$ 2(7 $-$ 9) $-$ 1( $-$ z $-$ 6) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $-$ 14 $-$ 3z + 4 + z + 6 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 2z = $-$ 4 $\Rightarrow$ z = $-$ 2

$\therefore$ x2 + y2 + z2 = 9

questions.question_text: If vectors $\vec{a_{1}}=x\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{a_{2}}=\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$ are collinear, then a possible unit vector parallel to the vector $x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$ is :
questions.question_html: If vectors $\vec{a_{1}}=x\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{a_{2}}=\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$ are collinear, then a possible unit vector parallel to the vector $x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$ is :
questions.explanation_text: $\vec{a_{2}}=\lambda\vec{a_{1}}$ $\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}=\lambda(x\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ $1=\lambda x,y=-\lambda,z=\lambda$ $x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}=\frac{1}{\lambda}\hat{i}-\lambda\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}$ Unit vector $=\frac{\frac{1}{\lambda}\hat{i}-\lambda\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{\lambda^{2}}+\lambda^{2}+\lambda^{2}}}$ $=\frac{\hat{i}-\lambda^{2}\hat{j}+\lambda^{2}\hat{k}}{\sqrt{1+2\lambda^{4}}}$ Let $\lambda^{2}=1$ , possible unit vector $=\frac{\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{3}}$
questions.explanation_html:
$\vec{a_{2}}=\lambda\vec{a_{1}}$

$\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}=\lambda(x\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})$

$1=\lambda x,y=-\lambda,z=\lambda$

$x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}=\frac{1}{\lambda}\hat{i}-\lambda\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}$

Unit vector $=\frac{\frac{1}{\lambda}\hat{i}-\lambda\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{\lambda^{2}}+\lambda^{2}+\lambda^{2}}}$

$=\frac{\hat{i}-\lambda^{2}\hat{j}+\lambda^{2}\hat{k}}{\sqrt{1+2\lambda^{4}}}$

Let $\lambda^{2}=1$ , possible unit vector $=\frac{\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.question_text: If $(\vec{a}+3\vec{b})$ is perpendicular to $(7\vec{a}-5\vec{b})$ and $(\vec{a}-4\vec{b})$ is perpendicular to $(7\vec{a}-2\vec{b})$ , then the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ (in degrees) is _______________.
questions.question_html: If $(\vec{a}+3\vec{b})$ is perpendicular to $(7\vec{a}-5\vec{b})$ and $(\vec{a}-4\vec{b})$ is perpendicular to $(7\vec{a}-2\vec{b})$ , then the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ (in degrees) is _______________.
questions.explanation_text: $(\vec{a}+3\vec{b})\perp(7\vec{a}-5\vec{b})$ $\therefore$ $(\vec{a}+3\vec{b}).(7\vec{a}-5\vec{b})=0$ $\Rightarrow$ $7|\vec{a}|^{2}-15|\vec{b}|^{2}+16\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ ....(1) Also, $(\vec{a}-4\vec{b}).(7\vec{a}-2\vec{b})=0$ $\Rightarrow$ $7|\vec{a}|^{2}+8|\vec{b}|^{2}-30\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ .....(2) Equation (1) × 30 $210|\vec{a}|^{2}-450|\vec{b}|^{2}+480\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ ....(3) Equation (2) × 16 $112|\vec{a}|^{2}+128|\vec{b}|^{2}-480\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ .....(4) from (3) & (4) $322|\vec{a}|^{2}=322|\vec{b}|^{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ $|\vec{a}|^{2}=|\vec{b}|^{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ $|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|$ From equation (2), $15|\vec{a}|=30\vec{a}.\vec{b}$ $\Rightarrow$ $15|\vec{a}|^{2}=30|\vec{a}|.|\vec{b}|cos\theta$ $cos\theta=\frac{15}{30}=\frac{1}{2}$ $\therefore$ $\theta=60^{\circ}$
questions.explanation_html:
$(\vec{a}+3\vec{b})\perp(7\vec{a}-5\vec{b})$

$\therefore$ $(\vec{a}+3\vec{b}).(7\vec{a}-5\vec{b})=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $7|\vec{a}|^{2}-15|\vec{b}|^{2}+16\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ ....(1)

Also, $(\vec{a}-4\vec{b}).(7\vec{a}-2\vec{b})=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $7|\vec{a}|^{2}+8|\vec{b}|^{2}-30\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ .....(2)

Equation (1) × 30

$210|\vec{a}|^{2}-450|\vec{b}|^{2}+480\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ ....(3)

Equation (2) × 16

$112|\vec{a}|^{2}+128|\vec{b}|^{2}-480\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ .....(4)

from (3) & (4)

$322|\vec{a}|^{2}=322|\vec{b}|^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $|\vec{a}|^{2}=|\vec{b}|^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|$

From equation (2),

$15|\vec{a}|=30\vec{a}.\vec{b}$

$\Rightarrow$ $15|\vec{a}|^{2}=30|\vec{a}|.|\vec{b}|cos\theta$

$cos\theta=\frac{15}{30}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ $\theta=60^{\circ}$

questions.question_text: If the shortest distance between the lines $\vec{r_{1}}=\alpha\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}+\lambda(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$ , $\lambda$ $\in$ R, $\alpha$ > 0 and $\vec{r_{2}}=-4\hat{i}-\hat{k}+\mu(3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-2\hat{k})$ , $\mu$ $\in$ R is 9, then $\alpha$ is equal to ____________.
questions.question_html: If the shortest distance between the lines $\vec{r_{1}}=\alpha\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}+\lambda(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$ , $\lambda$ $\in$ R, $\alpha$ > 0 and $\vec{r_{2}}=-4\hat{i}-\hat{k}+\mu(3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-2\hat{k})$ , $\mu$ $\in$ R is 9, then $\alpha$ is equal to ____________.
questions.explanation_text: If $\vec{r}=\vec{a}+\lambda\vec{b}$ and $\vec{r}=\vec{c}+\lambda\vec{d}$ then shortest distance between two lines is $L=\frac{(\vec{a}-\vec{c}).(\vec{b} \times \vec{d})}{|b \times d|}$ $\therefore$ $\vec{a}-\vec{c}=((\alpha+4)\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})$ $\frac{\vec{b} \times \vec{d}}{|b \times d|}=\frac{(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})}{3}$ $\therefore$ $((\alpha+4)\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}).\frac{(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})}{3}=9$ or $\alpha$ = 6
questions.explanation_html:
If $\vec{r}=\vec{a}+\lambda\vec{b}$ and $\vec{r}=\vec{c}+\lambda\vec{d}$ then shortest distance between two lines is

$L=\frac{(\vec{a}-\vec{c}).(\vec{b} \times \vec{d})}{|b \times d|}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{a}-\vec{c}=((\alpha+4)\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})$

$\frac{\vec{b} \times \vec{d}}{|b \times d|}=\frac{(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})}{3}$

$\therefore$ $((\alpha+4)\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}).\frac{(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})}{3}=9$

or $\alpha$ = 6

questions.question_text: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ . If the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are represented by the vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is $8\sqrt{3}$ square units, then $\vec{a}$ . $\vec{b}$ is equal to __________.
questions.question_html: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ . If the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are represented by the vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is $8\sqrt{3}$ square units, then $\vec{a}$ . $\vec{b}$ is equal to __________.
questions.explanation_text: $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ Area of parallelogram = $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$ $=|(\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+3\hat{k}) \times (3\hat{i}-\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k})|$ $8\sqrt{3}=|(4\alpha)\hat{i}+8\hat{j}-(4\alpha)\hat{k}|$ $(64)(3)=16\alpha^{2}+64+16\alpha^{2}$ $(64)(3)=32\alpha^{2}+64$ $6=\alpha^{2}+2$ $\alpha^{2}=4$ $\therefore$ $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ $\vec{a}.\vec{b}=3-\alpha^{2}+3$ $=6-\alpha^{2}$ $=6-4$ $=2$
questions.explanation_html:
$\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$

$\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k}$

Area of parallelogram = $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$

$=|(\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+3\hat{k}) \times (3\hat{i}-\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k})|$

$8\sqrt{3}=|(4\alpha)\hat{i}+8\hat{j}-(4\alpha)\hat{k}|$

$(64)(3)=16\alpha^{2}+64+16\alpha^{2}$

$(64)(3)=32\alpha^{2}+64$

$6=\alpha^{2}+2$

$\alpha^{2}=4$

$\therefore$ $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$

$\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k}$

$\vec{a}.\vec{b}=3-\alpha^{2}+3$

$=6-\alpha^{2}$

$=6-4$

$=2$

questions.explanation_text: $\vec{a}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{b}$ $\therefore$ $\vec{a}$ . $\vec{b}$ = 0 Given, | $\vec{a}$ $\times$ $\vec{b}$ | = | $\vec{a}$ | and | $\vec{a}$ | = | $\vec{b}$ | $\therefore$ | $\vec{a}$ $\times$ $\vec{b}$ | = | $\vec{a}$ | = | $\vec{b}$ | = k(assume) Now, angle between $\vec{a}$ and ( $\vec{a}$ + $\vec{b}$ + ( $\vec{a}$ $\times$ $\vec{b}$ )) $cos\theta=\frac{\vec{a}((\vec{a}+\vec{b}+(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}))}{|\vec{a}|.|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})|}$ $=\frac{|\vec{a}|^{2}+\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{a}(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})}{|\vec{a}|.|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})|}$ [Note $\vec{a}.(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})=[\vec{a}\vec{a}\vec{b}]=0$ ] $=\frac{|\vec{a}|^{2}+0+0}{|\vec{a}|.|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})|}$ Now, $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})|^{2}$ $=|\vec{a}|^{2}+|\vec{a}|^{2}+|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^{2}+$ $2\vec{a}.\vec{b}+2\vec{b}.(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})+2\vec{a}.(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ $=k^{2}+k^{2}+k^{2}$ $\therefore$ $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})|^{2}=3k^{2}$ $\Rightarrow |\vec{a}+\vec{b}+(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})|=\sqrt{3}k$ $\therefore$ $cos\theta=\frac{k^{2}}{k(\sqrt{3}k)}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ $\Rightarrow \theta=cos^{-1}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})$

$\therefore$ $\vec{x}=8(\frac{13}{8}\hat{i}-\frac{14}{8}\hat{j}+\frac{11}{8}\hat{k})$

$=13\hat{i}-14\hat{j}+11\hat{k}$

$|\vec{x}|^{2}=169+196+121=486$

questions.explanation_text: Given, $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ , $\vec{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}$ , $\vec{c}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ $\vec{r} \times \vec{a}=\vec{c} \times \vec{a}$ $\Rightarrow \vec{r} \times \vec{a}-\vec{c} \times \vec{a}=0$ $\Rightarrow (\vec{r}-\vec{c}) \times \vec{a}=0$ $\therefore$ $\vec{r}-\vec{c}=\lambda\vec{a}$ $\Rightarrow \vec{r}=\lambda\vec{a}+\vec{c}$ $\Rightarrow \vec{r}.\vec{b}=\lambda\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{c}.\vec{b}$ (taking dot with $\vec{b}$ ) $\Rightarrow 0=\lambda\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{c}.\vec{b}$ [ $\because$ $\vec{r}.\vec{b}=0$ ] $\Rightarrow \lambda(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}).(\hat{i}-\hat{j})+(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}).(\hat{i}-\hat{j})=0$ $\Rightarrow \lambda(1-2)+2=0$ $\Rightarrow \lambda=2$ $\therefore$ $\vec{r}=2\vec{a}+\vec{c}$ $\Rightarrow \vec{r}.\vec{a}=2\vec{a}.\vec{a}+\vec{c}.\vec{a}$ [taking dot with $\vec{a}$ ] $=2|\vec{a}|^{2}+\vec{a}.\vec{c}$ $=2(1+4+1)+(1-2+1)$ $\Rightarrow \vec{r}.\vec{a}=12$
questions.explanation_html:
Given, $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ ,

$\vec{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}$ ,

$\vec{c}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}$

$\vec{r} \times \vec{a}=\vec{c} \times \vec{a}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r} \times \vec{a}-\vec{c} \times \vec{a}=0$

$\Rightarrow (\vec{r}-\vec{c}) \times \vec{a}=0$

$\therefore$ $\vec{r}-\vec{c}=\lambda\vec{a}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}=\lambda\vec{a}+\vec{c}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}.\vec{b}=\lambda\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{c}.\vec{b}$ (taking dot with $\vec{b}$ )

$\Rightarrow 0=\lambda\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{c}.\vec{b}$ [ $\because$ $\vec{r}.\vec{b}=0$ ]

$\Rightarrow \lambda(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}).(\hat{i}-\hat{j})+(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}).(\hat{i}-\hat{j})=0$

$\Rightarrow \lambda(1-2)+2=0$

$\Rightarrow \lambda=2$

$\therefore$ $\vec{r}=2\vec{a}+\vec{c}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}.\vec{a}=2\vec{a}.\vec{a}+\vec{c}.\vec{a}$ [taking dot with $\vec{a}$ ]

$=2|\vec{a}|^{2}+\vec{a}.\vec{c}$

$=2(1+4+1)+(1-2+1)$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r}.\vec{a}=12$

questions.question_text: Let three vectors $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ be such that $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\vec{c}$ , $\vec{b} \times \vec{c}=\vec{a}$ and $|\vec{a}|=2$ . Then which one of the following is not true?
questions.question_html: Let three vectors $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ be such that $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\vec{c}$ , $\vec{b} \times \vec{c}=\vec{a}$ and $|\vec{a}|=2$ . Then which one of the following is not true?

options.label: B
options.html: Projection of $\vec{a}$ on $(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$ is 2

questions.explanation_text: (1) $\vec{a} \times ((\vec{b}+\vec{c}) \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}))$ $=\vec{a}(-\vec{b} \times \vec{c}+\vec{c} \times \vec{b})=-2(\vec{a} \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}))$ $=-2(\vec{a} \times \vec{a})=\vec{0}$ (2) Projection of $\vec{a}$ on $\vec{b} \times \vec{c}$ $=\frac{\vec{a}.(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})}{|\vec{b} \times \vec{c}|}=\frac{\vec{a}.\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}=|\vec{a}|=2$ (3) $[\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]+[\vec{c}\vec{a}\vec{b}]=2[\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]=2\vec{a}.(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$ $=2\vec{a}.\vec{a}=2|\vec{a}|^{2}=8$ (4) $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\vec{c}$ and $\vec{b} \times \vec{c}=\vec{a}$ $\Rightarrow \vec{a},\vec{b},\vec{c}$ are mutually $\perp$ vectors. $\therefore$ $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=|\vec{c}| \Rightarrow |\vec{a}||\vec{b}|=|\vec{c}| \Rightarrow |\vec{b}|=\frac{|\vec{c}|}{2}$ Also, $|\vec{b} \times \vec{c}|=|\vec{a}| \Rightarrow |\vec{b}||\vec{c}|=2 \Rightarrow |\vec{c}|=2$ & $|\vec{b}|=1$ $|3\vec{a}+\vec{b}-2\vec{c}|^{2}=(3\vec{a}+\vec{b}-2\vec{c}).(3\vec{a}+\vec{b}-2\vec{c})$ $=9|\vec{a}|^{2}+|\vec{b}|^{2}+4|\vec{c}|^{2}$ $=(9 \times 4)+1+(4 \times 4)$ $=36+1+16=53$
questions.explanation_html:
(1) $\vec{a} \times ((\vec{b}+\vec{c}) \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}))$

$=\vec{a}(-\vec{b} \times \vec{c}+\vec{c} \times \vec{b})=-2(\vec{a} \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}))$

$=-2(\vec{a} \times \vec{a})=\vec{0}$

(2) Projection of $\vec{a}$ on $\vec{b} \times \vec{c}$

$=\frac{\vec{a}.(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})}{|\vec{b} \times \vec{c}|}=\frac{\vec{a}.\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}=|\vec{a}|=2$

(3) $[\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]+[\vec{c}\vec{a}\vec{b}]=2[\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]=2\vec{a}.(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$

$=2\vec{a}.\vec{a}=2|\vec{a}|^{2}=8$

(4) $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\vec{c}$ and $\vec{b} \times \vec{c}=\vec{a}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{a},\vec{b},\vec{c}$ are mutually $\perp$ vectors.

$\therefore$ $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=|\vec{c}| \Rightarrow |\vec{a}||\vec{b}|=|\vec{c}| \Rightarrow |\vec{b}|=\frac{|\vec{c}|}{2}$

Also, $|\vec{b} \times \vec{c}|=|\vec{a}| \Rightarrow |\vec{b}||\vec{c}|=2 \Rightarrow |\vec{c}|=2$ & $|\vec{b}|=1$

$|3\vec{a}+\vec{b}-2\vec{c}|^{2}=(3\vec{a}+\vec{b}-2\vec{c}).(3\vec{a}+\vec{b}-2\vec{c})$

$=9|\vec{a}|^{2}+|\vec{b}|^{2}+4|\vec{c}|^{2}$

$=(9 \times 4)+1+(4 \times 4)$

$=36+1+16=53$

questions.explanation_text: Given $\vec{r}$ $\times$ $\vec{a}$ = $\vec{b}$ $\times$ $\vec{r}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\vec{r} \times \vec{a}=-\vec{r} \times \vec{b}$ $\vec{r} \times (\vec{a}+\vec{b})=0$ $\vec{r}||(\vec{a}+\vec{b})$ $\vec{r}=\lambda(\vec{a}+\vec{b})$ $(\vec{a}+\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$ $\because$ $\vec{r}.(2\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-\alpha\hat{k})=-1$ $\lambda[3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}].[2\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-\alpha\hat{k}]=-1$ $\Rightarrow \lambda(6-5-2\alpha)=-1$ $\lambda(1-2\alpha)=-1$ .... (1) $\vec{r}.(\alpha\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})=3$ $\lambda(3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}).(\alpha\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})=3$ $\Rightarrow \lambda[3\alpha-2+2]=3 \Rightarrow \lambda\alpha=1$ .... (2) From (1) & (2) $\lambda[1-\frac{2}{\lambda}]=-1$ $\lambda-2=-1 \Rightarrow \lambda=1\alpha=1$ $\vec{r}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ $\alpha+|\vec{r}|^{2}=1+14=15$
questions.explanation_html:
Given $\vec{r}$ $\times$ $\vec{a}$ = $\vec{b}$ $\times$ $\vec{r}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{r} \times \vec{a}=-\vec{r} \times \vec{b}$

$\vec{r} \times (\vec{a}+\vec{b})=0$

$\vec{r}||(\vec{a}+\vec{b})$

$\vec{r}=\lambda(\vec{a}+\vec{b})$

$(\vec{a}+\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$

$\because$ $\vec{r}.(2\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-\alpha\hat{k})=-1$

$\lambda[3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}].[2\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-\alpha\hat{k}]=-1$

$\Rightarrow \lambda(6-5-2\alpha)=-1$

$\lambda(1-2\alpha)=-1$ .... (1)

$\vec{r}.(\alpha\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})=3$

$\lambda(3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}).(\alpha\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})=3$

$\Rightarrow \lambda[3\alpha-2+2]=3 \Rightarrow \lambda\alpha=1$ .... (2)

From (1) & (2)

$\lambda[1-\frac{2}{\lambda}]=-1$

$\lambda-2=-1 \Rightarrow \lambda=1\alpha=1$

$\vec{r}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$

$\alpha+|\vec{r}|^{2}=1+14=15$

questions.question_text: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}-\alpha\hat{j}+\beta\hat{k}$ , $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}-\alpha\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=-\alpha\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ , where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are integers. questions.question_html: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}-\alpha\hat{j}+\beta\hat{k}$ ,    $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}-\alpha\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=-\alpha\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ , where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are integers. If $\vec{a}.\vec{b}=-1$ and $\vec{b}.\vec{c}=10$ , then $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}).\vec{c}$ is equal to ___________.
questions.explanation_text: $\vec{a}=(1,-\alpha,\beta)$ $\vec{b}=(3,\beta,-\alpha)$ $\vec{c}=(-\alpha,-2,1);\alpha,\beta \in I$ $\vec{a}.\vec{b}=-1 \Rightarrow 3-\alpha\beta-\alpha\beta=-1$ $\Rightarrow \alpha\beta=2$ Possible value of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ $\begin{aligned} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 \end{aligned}$ $\vec{b}.\vec{c}=10$ $\Rightarrow -3\alpha-2\beta-\alpha=10$ $\Rightarrow 2\alpha+\beta+5=0$ $\therefore$ $\alpha$ = $-$ 2; $\beta$ = $-$ 1 $[\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]=|\begin{aligned} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & -2 & 1 \end{aligned}|$ $=1(-1+4)-2(3-4)-1(-6+2)$ $=3+2+4=9$
questions.explanation_html:
$\vec{a}=(1,-\alpha,\beta)$

$\vec{b}=(3,\beta,-\alpha)$

$\vec{c}=(-\alpha,-2,1);\alpha,\beta \in I$

$\vec{a}.\vec{b}=-1 \Rightarrow 3-\alpha\beta-\alpha\beta=-1$

$\Rightarrow \alpha\beta=2$

Possible value of
$\alpha$ and $\beta$

$\begin{aligned} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 \end{aligned}$

$\vec{b}.\vec{c}=10$

$\Rightarrow -3\alpha-2\beta-\alpha=10$

$\Rightarrow 2\alpha+\beta+5=0$

$\therefore$ $\alpha$ = $-$ 2; $\beta$ = $-$ 1

$[\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]=|\begin{aligned} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & -2 & 1 \end{aligned}|$

$=1(-1+4)-2(3-4)-1(-6+2)$

$=3+2+4=9$

questions.question_text: For p > 0, a vector $\vec{v}_{2}=2\hat{i}+(p+1)\hat{j}$ is obtained by rotating the vector $\vec{v}_{1}=\sqrt{3}p\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ by an angle $\theta$ about origin in counter clockwise direction. questions.question_html: For p > 0, a vector $\vec{v}_{2}=2\hat{i}+(p+1)\hat{j}$ is obtained by rotating the vector $\vec{v}_{1}=\sqrt{3}p\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ by an angle $\theta$ about origin in counter clockwise direction. If $tan\theta=\frac{(\alpha\sqrt{3}-2)}{(4\sqrt{3}+3)}$ , then the value of $\alpha$ is equal to _____________.
questions.explanation_text: $|\vec{V_{1}}|=|\vec{V_{2}}|$ $3P^{2}+1=4+(P+1)^{2}$ $2P^{2}-2P-4=0 \Rightarrow P^{2}-P-2=0$ $P=2,-1$ (rejected) $cos\theta=\frac{\vec{V_{1}}.\vec{V_{2}}}{|\vec{V_{1}}||\vec{V_{2}}|}=\frac{2\sqrt{3}P+(P+1)}{\sqrt{(P+1)^{2}+4}\sqrt{3P^{2}+1}}$ $cos\theta=\frac{4\sqrt{3}+3}{\sqrt{13}\sqrt{13}}=\frac{4\sqrt{3}+3}{13}$ $tan\theta=\frac{\sqrt{112-24\sqrt{3}}}{4\sqrt{3}+3}=\frac{6\sqrt{3}-2}{4\sqrt{3}+3}=\frac{\alpha\sqrt{3}-2}{4\sqrt{3}+3}$ $\Rightarrow \alpha=6$
questions.explanation_html:
$|\vec{V_{1}}|=|\vec{V_{2}}|$

$3P^{2}+1=4+(P+1)^{2}$

$2P^{2}-2P-4=0 \Rightarrow P^{2}-P-2=0$

$P=2,-1$ (rejected)

$cos\theta=\frac{\vec{V_{1}}.\vec{V_{2}}}{|\vec{V_{1}}||\vec{V_{2}}|}=\frac{2\sqrt{3}P+(P+1)}{\sqrt{(P+1)^{2}+4}\sqrt{3P^{2}+1}}$

$cos\theta=\frac{4\sqrt{3}+3}{\sqrt{13}\sqrt{13}}=\frac{4\sqrt{3}+3}{13}$

$tan\theta=\frac{\sqrt{112-24\sqrt{3}}}{4\sqrt{3}+3}=\frac{6\sqrt{3}-2}{4\sqrt{3}+3}=\frac{\alpha\sqrt{3}-2}{4\sqrt{3}+3}$

$\Rightarrow \alpha=6$

$\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{b}.\vec{c}+\vec{c}.\vec{a}$ at x = x0 is :
questions.explanation_text: $f(x)=\vec{a}.(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$ $=[\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]$ $=|\begin{aligned} x & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & x & -1 \\ 7 & -2 & x \end{aligned}|$ $=x(x^{2}+2)+2(-2a+7)+3(4-7x)$ $\Rightarrow f(x)=x^{3}-27x+26$ $f^{'}(x)=3x^{2}-27$ For maxima or minima $f^{'}(x)=0$ $\therefore$ $3x^{2}-27=0$ $\Rightarrow x= \pm 3$ Now, $f^{''}(x)=6x$ f''(x) at x = $-$ 3 is 6( $-$ 3) = $-$ 18 < 0 $\therefore$ At x = $-$ 3 f(x) is maximum. So, x 0 = $-$ 3 $\therefore$ $\vec{a}=-3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ $\vec{b}=-2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ $\vec{c}=7\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$ Now, $\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{b}.\vec{c}+\vec{c}.\vec{a}$ $=(6+6-3)+(-14+6+3)+(-21+4-9)$ $=9-5-26$ $=-22$
questions.explanation_html:
$f(x)=\vec{a}.(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$

$=[\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]$

$=|\begin{aligned} x & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & x & -1 \\ 7 & -2 & x \end{aligned}|$

$=x(x^{2}+2)+2(-2a+7)+3(4-7x)$

$\Rightarrow f(x)=x^{3}-27x+26$

$f^{'}(x)=3x^{2}-27$

For maxima or minima $f^{'}(x)=0$

$\therefore$ $3x^{2}-27=0$

$\Rightarrow x= \pm 3$

Now, $f^{''}(x)=6x$

f''(x) at x = $-$ 3 is 6( $-$ 3) = $-$ 18 < 0

$\therefore$ At x = $-$ 3 f(x) is maximum.

So, x0 = $-$ 3

$\therefore$ $\vec{a}=-3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$

$\vec{b}=-2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-\hat{k}$

$\vec{c}=7\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$

Now, $\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{b}.\vec{c}+\vec{c}.\vec{a}$

$=(6+6-3)+(-14+6+3)+(-21+4-9)$

$=9-5-26$

$=-22$

questions.explanation_text: $|\vec{x}+\vec{y}|=|\vec{x}|$ Squaring both sides we get $|\vec{x}|^{2}+2\vec{x}.\vec{y}+|\vec{y}|^{2}=|\vec{x}|^{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ $2\vec{x}.\vec{y}+\vec{y}.\vec{y}$ = 0 ....(1) Given $2\vec{x}+\lambda\vec{y}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{y}$ $\therefore$ $(2\vec{x}+\lambda\vec{y}).\vec{y}$ = 0 $\Rightarrow$ $2\vec{x}.\vec{y}+\lambda\vec{y}.\vec{y}$ = 0 ....(2) Comparing (1) & (2) we get, $\lambda$ = 1

Let the position vectors of points 'A' and 'B' be $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ , respectively. A point
'P' divides the line segment AB internally in the
ratio $\lambda$ : 1 ( $\lambda$ > 0). If O is the origin and $\vec{OB}.\vec{OP}-3|\vec{OA} \times \vec{OP}|^{2}=6$ , then $\lambda$ is equal
to______.
questions.question_html:
Let the position vectors of points 'A' and 'B' be
$\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ , respectively. A point 'P' divides the line segment AB internally in the ratio $\lambda$ : 1 ( $\lambda$ > 0). If O is the origin and
$\vec{OB}.\vec{OP}-3|\vec{OA} \times \vec{OP}|^{2}=6$ , then $\lambda$ is equal to______.
questions.explanation_text: Let, $\vec{a}$ = $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}$ = $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ $\vec{OB}=\vec{b}$ $\vec{OP}=\frac{\vec{a}+\lambda\vec{b}}{1+\lambda}$ $\vec{OA}=\vec{a}$ $\therefore$ $\vec{OB}.\vec{OP}-3|\vec{OA} \times \vec{OP}|^{2}=6$ $\Rightarrow$ $\vec{b}.\frac{(\vec{a}+\lambda\vec{b})}{1+\lambda}-3|\vec{a} \times \frac{(\vec{a}+\lambda\vec{b})}{1+\lambda}|$ = 6 $\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\vec{b}.\vec{a}+\lambda(\vec{b}.\vec{b})}{1+\lambda}-3|\frac{\vec{a} \times \vec{a}+\lambda(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})}{1+\lambda}|$ = 6 [ $\vec{b}.\vec{a}$ = ( $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ ).( $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ ) = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 $\vec{b}.\vec{b}$ = ( $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ ).( $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ ) = 4 + 1 + 9 = 14 $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \end{aligned}|$ = (3 - 1) $\hat{i}$ - (3 - 2) $\hat{j}$ + (1 - 2) $\hat{k}$ = 2 $\hat{i}$ - $\hat{j}$ - $\hat{k}$ $\therefore$ $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$ = $\sqrt{2^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}$ = $\sqrt{6}$ ] $\Rightarrow$ $\frac{6+14\lambda}{1+\lambda}-3|\frac{\lambda(\sqrt{6})}{1+\lambda}|^{2}$ = 6 $\Rightarrow$ $\frac{6+14\lambda}{1+\lambda}-\frac{3\lambda^{2} \times 6}{(1+\lambda)^{2}}$ = 6 $\Rightarrow$ (14 $\lambda$ + 6)( $\lambda$ + 1)—18 $\lambda$ 2 = 6( $\lambda$ + 1) 2 $\Rightarrow$ —4 $\lambda$ 2 + 20 $\lambda$ + 6 = 6 $\lambda$ 2 + 12 $\lambda$ + 6 $\Rightarrow$ 10 $\lambda$ 2 — 8 $\lambda$ = 0 $\Rightarrow$ $\lambda$ (10 $\lambda$ — 8) = 0 As given $\lambda$ > 0 $\therefore$ $\lambda$ = $\frac{8}{10}$ = 0.8
questions.explanation_html:
Let, $\vec{a}$ = $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$

and $\vec{b}$ = $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$
$\vec{OB}=\vec{b}$

$\vec{OP}=\frac{\vec{a}+\lambda\vec{b}}{1+\lambda}$

$\vec{OA}=\vec{a}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{OB}.\vec{OP}-3|\vec{OA} \times \vec{OP}|^{2}=6$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{b}.\frac{(\vec{a}+\lambda\vec{b})}{1+\lambda}-3|\vec{a} \times \frac{(\vec{a}+\lambda\vec{b})}{1+\lambda}|$ = 6

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\vec{b}.\vec{a}+\lambda(\vec{b}.\vec{b})}{1+\lambda}-3|\frac{\vec{a} \times \vec{a}+\lambda(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})}{1+\lambda}|$ = 6

[ $\vec{b}.\vec{a}$ = ( $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ ).( $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ )

         = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6

$\vec{b}.\vec{b}$ = ( $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ ).( $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ )

         = 4 + 1 + 9 = 14

$\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=|\begin{aligned} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \end{aligned}|$

= (3 - 1) $\hat{i}$ - (3 - 2) $\hat{j}$ + (1 - 2) $\hat{k}$

= 2 $\hat{i}$ - $\hat{j}$ - $\hat{k}$

$\therefore$ $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$ = $\sqrt{2^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}$ = $\sqrt{6}$ ]

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{6+14\lambda}{1+\lambda}-3|\frac{\lambda(\sqrt{6})}{1+\lambda}|^{2}$ = 6

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{6+14\lambda}{1+\lambda}-\frac{3\lambda^{2} \times 6}{(1+\lambda)^{2}}$ = 6

$\Rightarrow$ (14 $\lambda$ + 6)( $\lambda$ + 1)—18 $\lambda$ 2 = 6( $\lambda$ + 1)2

$\Rightarrow$ —4 $\lambda$ 2 + 20 $\lambda$ + 6 = 6 $\lambda$ 2 + 12 $\lambda$ + 6

$\Rightarrow$ 10 $\lambda$ 2 — 8 $\lambda$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\lambda$ (10 $\lambda$ — 8) = 0

As given $\lambda$ > 0

$\therefore$ $\lambda$ = $\frac{8}{10}$ = 0.8

questions.question_text: Let a, b c $\in$ R be such that a 2 + b 2 + c 2 = 1. If $acos\theta=bcos(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3})=ccos(\theta+\frac{4\pi}{3})$ , where $\theta=\frac{\pi}{9}$ , then the angle between the vectors $a\hat{i}+b\hat{j}+c\hat{k}$ and $b\hat{i}+c\hat{j}+a\hat{k}$ is :
questions.question_html:
Let a, b c $\in$ R be such that a2 + b2 + c2 = 1. If
$acos\theta=bcos(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3})=ccos(\theta+\frac{4\pi}{3})$ ,
where $\theta=\frac{\pi}{9}$ , then the angle between the vectors $a\hat{i}+b\hat{j}+c\hat{k}$ and $b\hat{i}+c\hat{j}+a\hat{k}$ is :
questions.explanation_text: Let, $\vec{a_{1}}=a\hat{i}+b\hat{j}+c\hat{k}$ and $\vec{a_{2}}=b\hat{i}+c\hat{j}+a\hat{k}$ We know, Angle between two vectors $cos\alpha=\frac{\vec{a_{1}}.\vec{a_{2}}}{|\vec{a_{1}}|.|\vec{a_{2}}|}$ $=\frac{ab+bc+ac}{\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}.\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}}$ $=\frac{ab+bc+ac}{(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2})}$ Given, $a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=1$ $\therefore$ $cos\alpha=ab+bc+ac$ $=ab(\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c})$ .....(1) Given, $acos\theta=bcos(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3})=ccos(\theta+\frac{4\pi}{3})=\lambda$ (Assume) $\therefore$ $\frac{1}{a}=\frac{cos\theta}{\lambda}$ $\frac{1}{b}=\frac{cos(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3})}{\lambda}$ $\frac{1}{c}=\frac{cos(\theta+\frac{4\pi}{3})}{\lambda}$ $\therefore$ $\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}=\frac{1}{\lambda}[cos\theta+cos(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3})+cos(\theta+\frac{4\pi}{3})]$ $=\frac{1}{\lambda}[cos\theta+2cos(\frac{2\theta+2\pi}{2})cos(\frac{\frac{2\pi}{3}}{2})]$ $=\frac{1}{\lambda}[cos\theta+2cos(\theta+\pi)cos(\frac{\pi}{3})]$ $=\frac{1}{\lambda}[cos\theta+2(-cos\theta) \times \frac{1}{2}]$ $=\frac{1}{\lambda} \times 0$ $=0$ Putting value of $\lambda$ in equation (1), cos $\alpha$ = ab(0) = 0 $\Rightarrow$ $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{2}$
questions.explanation_html:
Let, $\vec{a_{1}}=a\hat{i}+b\hat{j}+c\hat{k}$

and $\vec{a_{2}}=b\hat{i}+c\hat{j}+a\hat{k}$

We know, Angle between two vectors

$cos\alpha=\frac{\vec{a_{1}}.\vec{a_{2}}}{|\vec{a_{1}}|.|\vec{a_{2}}|}$

$=\frac{ab+bc+ac}{\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}.\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}}$

$=\frac{ab+bc+ac}{(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2})}$

Given, $a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=1$

$\therefore$ $cos\alpha=ab+bc+ac$

$=ab(\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c})$ .....(1)

Given, $acos\theta=bcos(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3})=ccos(\theta+\frac{4\pi}{3})=\lambda$ (Assume)

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{a}=\frac{cos\theta}{\lambda}$

$\frac{1}{b}=\frac{cos(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3})}{\lambda}$

$\frac{1}{c}=\frac{cos(\theta+\frac{4\pi}{3})}{\lambda}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}=\frac{1}{\lambda}[cos\theta+cos(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3})+cos(\theta+\frac{4\pi}{3})]$

$=\frac{1}{\lambda}[cos\theta+2cos(\frac{2\theta+2\pi}{2})cos(\frac{\frac{2\pi}{3}}{2})]$

$=\frac{1}{\lambda}[cos\theta+2cos(\theta+\pi)cos(\frac{\pi}{3})]$

$=\frac{1}{\lambda}[cos\theta+2(-cos\theta) \times \frac{1}{2}]$

$=\frac{1}{\lambda} \times 0$

$=0$

Putting value of $\lambda$ in equation (1),

cos $\alpha$ = ab(0) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{2}$

If $\lambda=\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{b}.\vec{c}+\vec{c}.\vec{a}$ and $\vec{d}=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{b} \times \vec{c}+\vec{c} \times \vec{a}$ , then the ordered pair, $(\lambda,\vec{d})$ is equal to :
questions.question_html:
Let $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ be three unit vectors such that
$\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=\vec{0}$ . If $\lambda=\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{b}.\vec{c}+\vec{c}.\vec{a}$ and
$\vec{d}=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{b} \times \vec{c}+\vec{c} \times \vec{a}$ , then the ordered pair, $(\lambda,\vec{d})$ is equal to :
questions.explanation_text: $\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=\vec{0}$ $\Rightarrow$ $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}|^{2}$ = 0 $\Rightarrow$ $|\vec{a}|^{2}$ + $|\vec{b}|^{2}$ + $|\vec{c}|^{2}$ + $2(\vec{a}.\vec{b})$ + $2(\vec{b}.\vec{c})$ + $2(\vec{c}.\vec{a})$ = 0 $\Rightarrow$ 3 + $2(\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{b}.\vec{c}+\vec{c}.\vec{a})$ = 0 $\Rightarrow$ 3 + 2 $\lambda$ = 0 $\Rightarrow$ $\lambda$ = $-\frac{3}{2}$ $\vec{d}=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{b} \times \vec{c}+\vec{c} \times \vec{a}$ = $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{b} \times (-\vec{a}-\vec{b})+(-\vec{a}-\vec{b}) \times \vec{a}$ = $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}-\vec{b} \times \vec{a}+$ $\vec{b} \times \vec{b}-\vec{a} \times \vec{a}-\vec{b} \times \vec{a}$ = $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$ = $3(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$
questions.explanation_html:
$\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=\vec{0}$

$\Rightarrow$ $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}|^{2}$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $|\vec{a}|^{2}$ + $|\vec{b}|^{2}$ + $|\vec{c}|^{2}$ +
$2(\vec{a}.\vec{b})$ + $2(\vec{b}.\vec{c})$ + $2(\vec{c}.\vec{a})$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 3 + $2(\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{b}.\vec{c}+\vec{c}.\vec{a})$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 3 + 2 $\lambda$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\lambda$ = $-\frac{3}{2}$

$\vec{d}=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{b} \times \vec{c}+\vec{c} \times \vec{a}$

= $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{b} \times (-\vec{a}-\vec{b})+(-\vec{a}-\vec{b}) \times \vec{a}$

= $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}-\vec{b} \times \vec{a}+$ $\vec{b} \times \vec{b}-\vec{a} \times \vec{a}-\vec{b} \times \vec{a}$

= $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$

= $3(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

questions.question_text: If $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are unit vectors, then the greatest value of $\sqrt{3}|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|+|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|$ is_____.
questions.question_html:
If $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are unit vectors, then the greatest value of

$\sqrt{3}|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|+|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|$ is_____.
questions.explanation_text: Let angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ be $\theta$ . $\sqrt{3}|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|+|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|$ = $\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{1+1+2cos\theta})$ + $(\sqrt{1+1-2cos\theta})$ = $\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{2+2cos\theta})$ + $(\sqrt{2-2cos\theta})$ = $\sqrt{6}(\sqrt{1+cos\theta})$ + $\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{1-cos\theta})$ = $\sqrt{6}(\sqrt{2cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}})$ + $\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{2sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}})$ = $2\sqrt{3}|cos\frac{\theta}{2}|$ + 2 $|sin\frac{\theta}{2}|$ $\le$ $\sqrt{(2\sqrt{3})^{2}+(2)^{2}}$ = 4 Note : |x| = $\sqrt{x^{2}}$ |x - 1| = $\sqrt{(x-1)^{2}}$ |sin x| = $\sqrt{sin^{2}x}$ That is why $\sqrt{sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}}$ = $|sin\frac{\theta}{2}|$ and $\sqrt{cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}}$ = $|cos\frac{\theta}{2}|$
questions.explanation_html:
Let angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ be $\theta$ .

$\sqrt{3}|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|+|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|$

= $\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{1+1+2cos\theta})$ + $(\sqrt{1+1-2cos\theta})$

= $\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{2+2cos\theta})$ + $(\sqrt{2-2cos\theta})$

= $\sqrt{6}(\sqrt{1+cos\theta})$ + $\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{1-cos\theta})$

= $\sqrt{6}(\sqrt{2cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}})$ + $\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{2sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}})$

= $2\sqrt{3}|cos\frac{\theta}{2}|$ + 2 $|sin\frac{\theta}{2}|$

$\le$ $\sqrt{(2\sqrt{3})^{2}+(2)^{2}}$ = 4

Note : |x| = $\sqrt{x^{2}}$

|x - 1| = $\sqrt{(x-1)^{2}}$

|sin x| = $\sqrt{sin^{2}x}$

That is why $\sqrt{sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}}$ = $|sin\frac{\theta}{2}|$ and $\sqrt{cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}}$ = $|cos\frac{\theta}{2}|$

questions.question_html:
Let $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ be three unit vectors such that
$|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|^{2}$ + $|\vec{a}-\vec{c}|^{2}$ = 8.

Then $|\vec{a}+2\vec{b}|^{2}$ + $|\vec{a}+2\vec{c}|^{2}$ is equal to ______.
questions.explanation_html:
Given, $|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=|\vec{c}|=1$

$|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|^{2}$ + $|\vec{a}-\vec{c}|^{2}$ = 8

$\Rightarrow$ $|\vec{a}|^{2}+|\vec{b}|^{2}-2\vec{a}.\vec{b}+|\vec{a}|^{2}+|\vec{c}|^{2}-2\vec{a}.\vec{c}$ = 8

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{a}.\vec{c}$ = -2

Now, $|\vec{a}+2\vec{b}|^{2}$ + $|\vec{a}+2\vec{c}|^{2}$

= $|\vec{a}|^{2}+4|\vec{b}|^{2}+4\vec{a}.\vec{b}+|\vec{a}|^{2}+4|\vec{c}|^{2}+4\vec{a}.\vec{c}$

= 10 + 4 $(\vec{a}.\vec{b}+\vec{a}.\vec{c})$

= 10 + 4(-2)

= 2

–1 = –1 + m ...(2)

l = –m ...(3)

from (ii) m = 0

from (iii) $l$ = 0

Let the vectors $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ , $\vec{c}$ be such that $|\vec{a}|=2$ , $|\vec{b}|=4$ and $|\vec{c}|=4$ . If the projection of $\vec{b}$ on $\vec{a}$ is equal to the projection of $\vec{c}$ on $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$ ,
 then the value of $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}-\vec{c}|$ is ___________.
questions.question_html:
Let the vectors $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ , $\vec{c}$ be such that
$|\vec{a}|=2$ , $|\vec{b}|=4$ and $|\vec{c}|=4$ . If the projection of
$\vec{b}$ on $\vec{a}$ is equal to the projection of $\vec{c}$ on $\vec{a}$
and $\vec{b}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$ , then the value of
$|\vec{a}+\vec{b}-\vec{c}|$ is ___________.
questions.explanation_text: Projection of $\vec{b}$ on $\vec{a}$ = Projection of $\vec{c}$ on $\vec{a}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\vec{b}.\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}=\frac{\vec{c}.\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\vec{b}.\vec{a}=\vec{c}.\vec{a}$ $\because$ $\vec{b}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$ $\therefore$ $\vec{b}.\vec{c}=0$ Let $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}-\vec{c}|$ = k Square both sides k 2 = $(\vec{a})^{2}$ + $(\vec{b})^{2}$ + $(\vec{c})^{2}$ + $2\vec{a}.\vec{b}$ - $2\vec{b}.\vec{c}$ - $2\vec{a}.\vec{c}$ $\Rightarrow$ k 2 = $(\vec{a})^{2}$ + $(\vec{b})^{2}$ + $(\vec{c})^{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ k 2 = 2 2 + 4 2 + 4 2 = 36 $\Rightarrow$ k = 6
questions.explanation_html:
Projection of $\vec{b}$ on $\vec{a}$ = Projection of $\vec{c}$ on $\vec{a}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\vec{b}.\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}=\frac{\vec{c}.\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{b}.\vec{a}=\vec{c}.\vec{a}$

$\because$ $\vec{b}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{b}.\vec{c}=0$

Let $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}-\vec{c}|$ = k

Square both sides

k2 = $(\vec{a})^{2}$ + $(\vec{b})^{2}$ + $(\vec{c})^{2}$ + $2\vec{a}.\vec{b}$ - $2\vec{b}.\vec{c}$ - $2\vec{a}.\vec{c}$

$\Rightarrow$ k2 = $(\vec{a})^{2}$ + $(\vec{b})^{2}$ + $(\vec{c})^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ k2 = 22 + 42 + 42 = 36

$\Rightarrow$ k = 6

questions.question_text: If the volume of a parallelopiped, whose coterminus edges are given by the vectors $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+n\hat{k}$ , $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-n\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=\hat{i}+n\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ ( $n \ge 0$ ), is 158 cu. units, then :
questions.question_html:
If the volume of a parallelopiped, whose
coterminus edges are given by the
vectors $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+n\hat{k}$ ,
$\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-n\hat{k}$ and
$\vec{c}=\hat{i}+n\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ ( $n \ge 0$ ), is 158 cu. units, then :
questions.explanation_text: We know, Volume(V) = $[\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]$ $\Rightarrow$ 158 = $|\begin{aligned} 1 & 1 & n \\ 2 & 4 & -n \\ 1 & n & 3 \end{aligned}|$ $\Rightarrow$ (12 + n 2 ) – (6 + n) + n(2n–4)=158 $\Rightarrow$ 3n 2 –5n + 6 –158 = 0 $\Rightarrow$ 3n 2 – 5n – 152 = 0 $\Rightarrow$ 3n 2 – 24n + 19n – 152 = 0 $\Rightarrow$ (3n + 19) (n–8) = 0 $\Rightarrow$ n = 8, $-\frac{19}{3}$ (rejected) $\therefore$ $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+8\hat{k}$ , $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-8\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ Now $\vec{a}.\vec{c}$ = 1 + 8 + 24 = 33 $\vec{b}.\vec{c}$ = 2 + 32 - 24 = 10
questions.explanation_html:
We know, Volume(V) = $[\vec{a}\vec{b}\vec{c}]$

$\Rightarrow$ 158 = $|\begin{aligned} 1 & 1 & n \\ 2 & 4 & -n \\ 1 & n & 3 \end{aligned}|$

$\Rightarrow$ (12 + n2) – (6 + n) + n(2n–4)=158

$\Rightarrow$ 3n2 –5n + 6 –158 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 3n2 – 5n – 152 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 3n2 – 24n + 19n – 152 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ (3n + 19) (n–8) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ n = 8, $-\frac{19}{3}$ (rejected)

$\therefore$ $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+8\hat{k}$ ,

$\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-8\hat{k}$ and

$\vec{c}=\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$

Now $\vec{a}.\vec{c}$ = 1 + 8 + 24 = 33

$\vec{b}.\vec{c}$ = 2 + 32 - 24 = 10
